definitions.meaning: first meaning: an association of people who meet for a shared interest
second meaning: a playing card of the black suit marked with a trefoil

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it suggests a membership card for a society; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an organised association of members and one of the four suits in a pack of playing cards.

indicators.note: rebuilt means put together in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old path is reconstructed to serve as a memorial.
explanation.definitionFit: A cenotaph is a war memorial honouring people buried elsewhere.

parts.note: a set is a group of things

explanation.surface: Someone tells you to unsettle a happy gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset someone is to trouble or agitate them.

clue.text: Killer has got in behind two idiots

indicators.note: the little word comes behind, after, the pair of fools

parts.note: an ass is a fool, and two of them sit side by side

explanation.surface: A murderer has slipped in at the back of a pair of fools.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a murderer, especially one who kills a prominent person for hire or politics.

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, so the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: a golfer addressing the ball is lining up to it, looking at it

explanation.surface: A cook trims a condiment while eyeing up the sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Condiment' looks like the definition but is just wordplay; the definition is at the other end.
explanation.definitionFit: Salad dressing is a sauce such as vinaigrette poured over salad leaves.

parts.note: someone from the Scottish Highlands is a Scot

explanation.surface: A member of the royal family has an encounter with a man from the Highlands.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Ascot is the famous royal race meeting in Berkshire; 'meeting' is a horse-racing fixture, not an encounter.
explanation.definitionFit: The racecourse hosts the summer race meeting attended by the monarch, called Royal Ascot.

indicators.note: done awfully, badly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A pragmatic person is very annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' reads as angry, but it is the diagonal cross, as on the Scottish flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A saltire is a diagonal X-shaped cross, the St Andrew's cross on Scotland's flag.

parts.note: a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Twelve of something definitely not functioning.
explanation.definitionFit: Noon is twelve o'clock midday.

clue.text: Brown carries drink for US president

indicators.note: the colour carries the drink inside it

explanation.surface: Someone called Brown brings a drink to the American president.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown capitalised looks like a surname, perhaps Gordon Brown; it is just a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry S. Truman was the 33rd President of the United States.

clue.text: Punched by right, bewildered Liston gets breathing space

indicators.note: the jumbled boxer's name is struck into by the letter for right, which ends up inside it
a bewildered boxer is scrambled, so the letters of the name are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written; Sonny Liston was a heavyweight boxer

explanation.surface: Boxer Sonny Liston, dazed by a right-hander, gets a moment to catch his breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breathing space' looks like a pause in the fight, but here it is literal: a space you breathe through.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostril is one of the two openings of the nose through which air passes, literally a space for breathing.

clue.text: Instrument in small room with leader of orchestra

parts.note: a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here the start of orchestra

explanation.surface: An instrument kept in a little room alongside the orchestra's leader.
explanation.definitionFit: The cello is a large bowed string instrument of the violin family, played seated.

clue.text: Sign on pole installed in grotto, temporarily

indicators.note: the answer sits installed inside the run of letters across these two words

parts.note: the answer spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A sign on a pole is set up for a while inside a cave.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an emblem of a clan, typically carved on a tall wooden pole.

indicators.note: a new version of these words is a rearranged one

explanation.surface: A fresh contract comes with this as a feature.
explanation.definitionFit: A detail is a particular item or characteristic, a feature of something.

indicators.note: extraordinary suggests out of the ordinary order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ice skater is an exceptional star performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'star' looks like a celebrity, but it is the printed symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: An asterisk is the small star-shaped printing symbol, its name from Greek for little star.

clue.text: Crunchy snack, man eating raisins primarily with nuts

indicators.note: the chess piece swallows the letter, so it goes inside

parts.note: a chess man, the lowliest piece

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of the following word

parts.note: nuts and crackers both mean crazy

explanation.surface: A chap munching raisins with nuts on the side as a crunchy snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man' and 'nuts' look like a person snacking on nuts; man is a chess piece, and nuts means mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Prawn crackers are light, crisp puffed snacks flavoured with shrimp, served with Chinese meals.

parts.note: a tissue is used for wiping things clean

explanation.surface: A cleaner is involved in a quarrel at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter that is at issue is the point under debate or being contested.

indicators.note: a failed arrangement has broken down, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An old socialist leader let down the people of Croatia.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidel Castro was the communist revolutionary who led Cuba for decades.

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: to talk about something is to discuss it

explanation.surface: An occasion that people will mostly want to chat about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Event' sounds like any happening, but here it is a sporting event in athletics.
explanation.definitionFit: The discus throw is a field event in athletics, contested at the Olympics.

clue.text: Skip exercise when carried by vehicle

indicators.note: the exercise is carried inside the vehicle

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Someone skips their workout because they are being driven around.
explanation.definitionFit: To caper is to skip or dance about playfully.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a constituent part of the USA, here the two outside the mainland
second meaning: to declare or express in words

explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example', tagging the definition; it is a second definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are US member territories with their own governments, and the verb also means to declare formally.

indicators.note: the zone goes around the letter for northern

explanation.surface: A zone surrounding a stadium up in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed venue for sports or shows, effectively a stadium.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a permit allowing entry
second meaning: what a quiz contestant says when unable to answer

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense comes from quiz shows such as Mastermind, where a contestant who doesn't know says this word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pass is a ticket or permit granting admission, and in quizzes it means declining to answer.

clue.text: Ape so different, he wrote about tortoise and hare

definitions.text: he wrote about tortoise and hare

indicators.note: made different, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ape behaving unusually, with a nod to the author of a famous animal race tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek fabulist credited with The Tortoise and the Hare.

clue.text: Native of Jaffa for example is right, a lie wrong

indicators.note: put wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone from Jaffa says a claim is correct and that a lie is mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: Jaffa is an ancient port city, now part of Tel Aviv.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaffa lies in that Middle Eastern country, so someone born there is a citizen of it.

clue.text: Part of ship always hidden by raised platform

indicators.note: the word is concealed within the platform, so it goes inside

parts.note: a stage is a raised platform for performers
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A section of the vessel is permanently tucked under a raised deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' looks like it might turn the platform round, but it simply describes the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage was the cheapest passenger accommodation on a ship, originally near the rudder.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: in return, as in phoning or paying someone in turn

explanation.walkthrough: The two definitions are separate senses of one short word: a verb and an adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: To support a candidate is to endorse them; the adverb sense means in return, as in writing to someone in reply.
